summary: Dayong (1893–1929) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Puren Bai, and Dorje Geshe, later teaching at Wuchang Buddhist Institute in 1923.

Debala Mitra (1925–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Dineschandra Sircar (~1946–1952). She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded and served as Director of the Central Institute of Indian Languages (~1969–1989) and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research (~2013).

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) worked in philosophy and Indology. He earned his B.A. at the University of Calcutta (~1935–1939) and studied under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1943–1956), and was a guest professor at Calcutta.
Deborah Carlson is a scholar in history and archaeology with posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology, both attested in 2015.

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian and Tibetologist who earned a PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar (~1971–1976) and habilitated at the University of Vienna. She held the Asian art history chair at Vienna (1994–2015) after teaching at UCLA (1978–1985).
Declan Quigley (born 1956) works in Indology and religious studies. He has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei (born 1968) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998), where he became an associate professor of religious studies around 1998.
Demchok Dorje was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Denis Sinor (1916–2011) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied under Paul Pelliot (~1939–1944) and at Cambridge (~1948), later holding posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (Director, 1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett (1925–2006) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at SOAS and St Catharine's College. He held the Chair of Chinese at the University of London (1960–1968) and Cambridge (1968–1980), ending his career at Princeton (1980–1994).

Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a linguist who studied at the École des chartes (~1941–1945) and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1946–1950). She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1960–1990).

Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928–2014) studied at Drepung Loseling and Gyume Tantric College. Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he was a research fellow at the University of Calcutta (~1967–1969), principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and Abbot of Namgyal Monastery (1986–1991).

Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where he studied under M.A. supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).

Dennis Hirota (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at UC Berkeley and a Ph.D. at Nagoya University. He worked at the Hongwanji International Center (~1974–1993) and was a professor at Ryukoku University (~1993–2016).
Dennis Hudson (1938–2006) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who served as a professor in the Department of Religion and Biblical Studies at Smith College, attested from 1987 to 2000.

Denzaburo Yoshizawa (1924–2003) was a philosopher who studied under Tetsuro Watsuji at the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948). He held posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1953–1988) and Iryo Sosei University (~1989–1997).

Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He has taught at Virginia, UNC Greensboro, and East Carolina University, where he co-directed the Religious Studies Program (attested 2010).

Dermot Killingley (born 1935) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS. He held posts at the University of Malaya (1961–1968) and Newcastle University (~1970–2000), where he served as Reader.

Dermott Joseph Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned a BA at Trinity College Dublin (2003), an MA at Leiden University (2009), and a PhD at UCLA (2018) under doctoral supervisor William M. Bodiford.
